title: Gabriel, cardinal de Gramont, Rome, to Montmorency, 21 July 1530, BnF fr. 3071 no. 7 f. 17 (catalogue item 6, Gramont's cipher 1530)

plaintext.source: No decipherment found. Lasry decoded the text in 2023, unpublished.

transcription.notes: 14 Nov 2026: 13 cipher lines transcribed sign by sign (texts/gramont1530_transcription.txt), 536 signs = 552 tokens by --measure --drop-first less 16 separator marks; a single AI transcription, not checked by a person. The first reading (18 Sept) counted 14 lines and kept no alias file.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on graphic signs, two to seven homophones per letter, LL/RR/SS signs, COM and CON signs, a few code signs and nulls ('Gramont's cipher (1530)', Lasry's table for fr. 3071 f. 17; Tomokiyo's sibling fr. 3019 f. 20).
system.sibling_key: Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' (GL.htm, GL/BnF_fr3071_f17.png; copy img/BnF_fr3071_f17.png); Tomokiyo's table from fr. 3019 f. 20 (img/francisGramont.png).
system.notes: Lasry's table lists five unknown signs; two identified here from context: 8Δ = pape, key-ring sign = roy; the 18 Sept reading of ʃʃ on a stem as a word-initial null is not confirmed by the 14 Nov 2026 sign transcription (it stands between 'le' and Z̄). g serves B, V and E. Homophone maxima counted from Lasry's table as transcribed in fr3071_no7_gramont.md (R has 7 forms incl. ligatures; O has 4).

prior_solution.where: Key published online by Lasry (table dated 4-5 Nov 2023 on cryptiana GL.htm). Lasry also decoded this letter in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue item; no target-specific intervention recorded. Relayed Lasry's 21 Sept 2026 correction on his unpublished decipherments.

solution.what: Matched the four items against Tomokiyo's francis.htm and GL.htm: four letters, four different keys, all tabulated by Lasry in 2023; no plaintext on either site.
Located the correct Gallica arks (fr. 3091 is btv1b9060253s, not the catalogue's) and fetched full-resolution canvases.
Applied Lasry's 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' table to the 14 cipher lines of f. 17r by eye from line strips.
Read about 85 % of the cipher; identified three of Lasry's five unknown signs (8Δ = pape, key-ring = roy, ʃʃ-on-stem null). Ends of lines 1-2 and the middle of lines 5-7 at lower confidence.
Dated to 21 July 1530 by the return of the Queen and the princes (Bidassoa, 1 July 1530) and Rodolfo Pio's mission as nuncio.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded all four texts in 2023 when reconstructing the keys, but the decipherments were never published. Prior-solution record updated: a reading existed, unpublished, learned of after the reading and not used (only his keys were).

Split the combined catalogue item 6 entry under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): four letters in four keys. gramont1529 keeps fr. 3091 no. 23 (Gramont's cipher 1529); langeac1529 takes fr. 3083 no. 8 (Avranches' cipher 1); gramont1530 takes fr. 3071 no. 7 (Gramont's cipher 1530); the Mâcon letter fr. 3071 no. 4 moved to rome1536 with the other letters in Mascon's cipher. This entry is fr3071_no7_gramont.md, moved from targets/gramont1529/.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): gramont1530: reading fr3071_no7_gramont.md linked; key = Lasry's table image img/BnF_fr3071_f17.png and texts/key.md (copied verbatim from the reading file). No ciphertext transcription exists in the folder.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Full-texts audit (section I): no transcription of the cipher was in the folder and none exists elsewhere (no DECODE record named; Lasry's decipherment unpublished). Fetched the leaf from openapi.bnf.fr (IIIF, btv1b9060315f view 30, 4352 x 6081 px) and transcribed the cipher block sign by sign on native-resolution strips: 13 lines, 536 signs, shape labels matched to Lasry's table (texts/gramont1530_transcription.txt). Single AI transcription, not checked by a person; look-alike pairs listed in the file header.

Decoded the transcription mechanically with Lasry's table (texts/gramont1530_decode.md): continuous French over all 13 lines; 532 of 536 signs take a value. The sign 4t reads 'et' at its four places; the COM sign writes con- and com-. Gaps of the 18 Sept reading filled (line 2 'ie suis apres pour le faire mectre a dev[.]e execution'; lines 6-7 'seul pour scavoir quel il y faict et me semble qu'il n'i a que rien'), and 'recepvoir' corrected to 'concepvoir'. Without a value: ʃʃ, Z̄, #, ▣. The earlier note that ʃʃ is a word-initial null is not confirmed: it stands between 'le' and Z̄.

Rewrote the cipher block of fr3071_no7_gramont_reading.md and fr3071_no7_gramont_en.md from the decode; read share 0.961 (245 words, 10 holes, v10 measure; 0.933 before). Entry state read in part -> read with a reading review (grade A); fraction_read 0.85 estimated -> 0.993 measured (532/536 signs). outcome.class left at 'read in part' for the maintainer to decide: the transcription has not been checked by a person.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' for this letter (cryptiana GL.htm); no new cryptanalysis.
outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/gramont1530_decode.md: 532 of the 536 transcribed cipher signs decode to a letter or word that reads in its sentence (4 signs without a value: ʃʃ, Z̄, #, ▣); 14 Nov 2026. The 18 Sept figure was an estimate of about 85 %.

gaps.item: four signs without a value: ʃʃ and Z̄ (line 1, between 'le' and 'vouloir'), # (line 2, between 'iamais' and 'ie suis'), ▣ (line 2, in 'dev[▣] execution')
gaps.detail: each occurs once in this letter; ʃʃ, Z̄ and # are among the five signs Lasry's table leaves unknown, and ▣ is X in his table, which does not fit the word here; no gloss, clear copy or decipherment of this letter exists. The other letters in this key (fr. 3019 f. 20, fr. 3040 ff. 12, 18, fr. 2980 nos. 21-22) are the place to fix them.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3071 no. 7, f. 17, Rome, 21 July [1530]
texts.summary: Gramont, cardinal, writes from Rome to Montmorency: the Pope keeps "Francisque" on the mission rather than Gramont, for fear of Imperial suspicion; Rodolfo Pio, bishop of Faenza and nephew of Carpi, is to leave in 3-4 days to congratulate the King on the return of the Queen and the princes (handed over at the Bidassoa, 1 July 1530).
texts.note: 14 Nov 2026: the 13 cipher lines transcribed sign by sign from the Gallica IIIF image (536 signs; a single AI transcription, not checked by a person) and decoded mechanically with Lasry's table (texts/gramont1530_decode.md); the reading and the English follow that decode. Four signs have no value ([ʃʃ], [Z̄], [#], [▣]); three signs are doubtful. fr3071_no7_gramont.md is the first reading by eye (18 Sept 2026, about 85%). Lasry's own 2023 decipherment is unpublished and not in the repository. Read share 0.961 of the words of fr3071_no7_gramont_reading.md (v10 measure: 245 words, 10 holes), the holes being the four signs, the two word signs in brackets and the clear close, transcribed only in fragments.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences after the re-decode: the cipher block is continuous French from 'vouloir est tousiours bon' to 'de messeigneurs', every letter carried by a transcribed sign and Lasry's table (g chosen between b, v and e by the word); holes are four signs without a value and the fragmentary clear close. Not checked against any other decipherment: none is available.
